Hi Alex,

I'm so excited that you're coming next month! If I were you, I'd spend a few days in Hoi An, because the old town is beautiful at night, and then go to Da Nang for the beaches.

The weather will probably be hot and humid, so pack light clothes, sun cream and a hat. It might rain in the afternoon, so an umbrella would be useful too.

I'd love to show you around Hue, where I live. Let me know which dates work for you.

See you soon,
Minh

Hi Jamie,

Thanks for your email. I'm sorry you're feeling stressed – I felt exactly the same before my exams last year, so I know how hard it is.

My advice is to make a realistic timetable and study in short sessions of about forty minutes, with breaks in between. Also, try not to stay up late, because you'll remember much more if you get enough sleep.

Why don't you go for a swim or a walk every afternoon? Exercise really helps you clear your mind.

Good luck – I know you'll do well!
Nam

Hi Chris,

You asked about Vietnamese food, so I'd definitely recommend Bep Me, a small family restaurant near the river. It isn't fancy, but it's always busy, which is a good sign!

You should try the grilled pork with rice noodles, which is their speciality, and the fresh spring rolls. If you like spicy food, the beef salad is excellent too.

It's quite cheap – about ten dollars per person – but it gets very crowded at weekends, so I'd book a table in advance or go early.

Enjoy!
Linh

Hi everyone,

I'm thinking of starting an English conversation club, and I'd love to know if anyone would like to join. Many of us use English with clients, but we don't get much chance to practise speaking in a relaxed way.

A Perfect Weekend in Saigon

Saigon is a city that never sleeps, so there's always something to do. On Saturday morning, start with a strong iced coffee at a pavement café and watch the motorbikes go by. Then visit the War Remnants Museum, which is moving and very informative.

In the evening, take a walk along Nguyen Hue walking street, where families and street performers gather. After that, head to District 4 for some of the best seafood in the city.

What makes a weekend here special is the energy. Although it can be noisy, the friendly people and delicious food will make you want to come back.

Why Everyone Should Learn to Cook

Many students live on instant noodles and takeaways, but learning to cook is one of the most useful skills you can have.

Firstly, cooking at home is much healthier. You know exactly what is in your food, so you can use less salt, sugar and oil. Secondly, it saves a lot of money. A home-cooked meal often costs less than half the price of a takeaway.

If you're a beginner, start with simple dishes like fried rice or omelettes. Watch online videos, and don't worry about mistakes – everyone burns something at first! Soon you'll be inviting friends round for dinner.

The Teacher Who Believed in Me

When I was fourteen, I was failing almost every subject, and I had completely lost interest in school. Then Mr Long became my form teacher.

Instead of punishing me for my bad results, he asked me what I was interested in. When I told him I loved drawing, he encouraged me to design posters for school events. For the first time, I felt that I was good at something.

Slowly, my confidence grew, and my grades improved too. Today I work as a graphic designer, and I often think that without Mr Long, I would never have found my passion.

Ba Be: Vietnam's Hidden Lake

Most tourists heading north go straight to Ha Long Bay or Sapa, but if you want peace and quiet, you should visit Ba Be National Park instead.

The park is home to a beautiful lake surrounded by forested mountains and small villages. Visitors can take a boat trip through caves, kayak on the calm water or stay overnight in a traditional wooden house with a local family.

The park is about six hours by bus from Hanoi, so it's best to stay for at least two nights. Bring warm clothes in winter, as the evenings can be surprisingly cold.

items.sampleAnswer:
Are We Too Dependent on Our Phones?

Look around any café or bus and you'll see the same thing: almost everyone is staring at a screen. We use our phones to work, shop, chat and even find our way home.

In my opinion, we have become too dependent on them. Many people feel anxious if they leave their phone at home, and constant notifications make it hard to concentrate. We also spend less time talking face to face.

There are some simple solutions, though. Try turning off notifications, keeping your phone out of the bedroom and having phone-free meals with your family. You might be surprised how much better you feel.

The Mid-Autumn Festival

The Mid-Autumn Festival takes place on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month, when the moon is at its brightest. Traditionally, it was a time for farmers to celebrate the end of the harvest, but today it is mostly a festival for children.

In the weeks before, shops are full of colourful lanterns and mooncakes filled with lotus seeds or egg yolk. On the night itself, children carry lanterns through the streets, and there are lion dances everywhere.

For me, it is a special time because my whole family sits together, eats mooncakes and watches the moon, just as we did when I was small.

The Last Lighthouse tells the story of a young woman who moves to a remote island to look after a lighthouse after her father's death. While she is there, she discovers letters that reveal a family secret.

Last Saturday, I went to the Sunset Sounds Festival, which was held on the beach for the first time this year. Around five thousand people came to watch eight bands perform as the sun went down over the sea.

The highlight was definitely the final band, who played all their famous songs while fireworks lit up the sky. The atmosphere was fantastic, and everyone was singing along.

However, the organisation could have been better. The queues for food and drinks were extremely long, and there weren't enough toilets. If they fix these problems, next year's festival will be even better.

Nowadays, almost every student owns a smartphone, so many schools are discussing whether phones should be allowed in class.

On the one hand, phones can be useful learning tools. Students can look up words, do online quizzes and research topics quickly. Teachers can also use apps to make lessons more interactive.

On the other hand, phones are a big distraction. Many students are tempted to check social media or play games instead of listening. Phones can also make it easier to cheat in tests.

In my opinion, phones should only be allowed when the teacher asks students to use them for a specific activity. This way, students get the benefits without the distractions.

Traffic jams and air pollution are serious problems in many big cities, and some people believe the solution is to ban cars from city centres completely.

There are clear benefits to this idea. The air would be cleaner, the streets would be quieter and safer for pedestrians, and there would be more space for parks and cafés. People might also walk or cycle more, which is good for their health.

However, a ban could cause problems for elderly or disabled people, as well as for businesses that need to deliver goods. Public transport would also need to improve a lot.

Overall, I agree with the idea, but only if cities first provide cheap, reliable buses and trains for everyone.

More and more young people dream of running their own business instead of working for a company. But is it really the better choice?

Being self-employed has many advantages. You can choose your own hours, make your own decisions and keep all the profits. For creative people, this freedom can be very motivating.

On the other hand, working for a company offers security. Employees receive a regular salary, paid holidays and health insurance. They can also learn from experienced colleagues and don't have to worry about finding customers.

In my view, neither option is better for everyone. It depends on a person's personality and situation. I think it is wise to gain experience in a company first and then start a business later.

Since the pandemic, online learning has become a normal part of education. Some people now claim that it is just as effective as learning in a classroom.

Online learning certainly has advantages. Students can study at their own speed, watch lessons again and save time travelling. It also allows people in remote areas to take courses from the best universities.

However, classroom learning offers things that are difficult to replace. Students can ask questions immediately, work in groups and build friendships. Many learners also find it hard to stay motivated when they study alone at home.

Personally, I believe a mix of both is ideal. Online materials are great for practice, but face-to-face lessons are still essential for motivation and communication.

It is often said that young people today are less healthy than their parents were at the same age. There is some truth in this, but the situation is more complicated.

On the one hand, many teenagers spend hours sitting in front of screens instead of playing outside. Fast food and sugary drinks are also cheaper and easier to find than they used to be, which has led to more obesity.

On the other hand, young people today know much more about health. Many go to the gym, follow fitness accounts online and smoke far less than previous generations did.

In conclusion, I think young people are not necessarily less healthy, but they face different risks. Schools and families should encourage them to stay active.

Report on the Staff Canteen

Introduction
The aim of this report is to describe staff opinions of the canteen and suggest improvements. I spoke to twenty colleagues.

Positive points
Most staff think the food is reasonably priced and that the canteen is clean. The rice dishes are particularly popular.

Problems
However, many people complained that the menu rarely changes and that there are few vegetarian options. The canteen is also very crowded between 12 and 1.

Recommendations
I recommend introducing a weekly menu with at least two vegetarian dishes. Staggered lunch breaks would also reduce queues.

Report on Sports Facilities for Young People

Introduction
This report looks at the sports facilities available to teenagers in Thanh Xuan district and suggests some improvements.

Current facilities
There is a public swimming pool, two football pitches and several outdoor gyms in the parks. The pool is popular, but it is quite expensive for students.

Problems
